The market for short-term funds, usually up to one year (deposits, treasury bills, short-term loans).
The market for long-term finance of more than a year (shares, bonds, long-term loans).
Primary: new shares and bonds are first sold. Secondary: existing securities are traded between investors, which makes them easier to sell.
A market in which shares and other securities of listed companies are bought and sold; listing helps raise capital but brings rules and disclosure.
Accept deposits, give loans and overdrafts, and provide payment services; the main source of short-term business finance.

front: African Development Bank and World Bank
back: Support development projects in African countries (AfDB) and development and poverty reduction (World Bank) through loans, grants and support.
